_how_to_use: Every repo you own and have starred on GitHub shows up in the app automatically. Add an entry here (keyed by repo name) to give it a nicer title, a domain, optional extra domains ('also', used by the domain filter), a headline result and a stack. 'featured_order' sets the order in the default view; the first 'lead_count' of them get large lead cards. Optional 'page' (an in-app page key, e.g. 'power-test' or 'agent-runs') and 'page_label' add a button that opens that page.

park-crowd-forecast.title: Crowd Forecast and Staffing Optimizer
park-crowd-forecast.result: Forecasts daily crowds at Universal Orlando's parks 90 days out on Databricks and feeds them to a mixed-integer program (OR-Tools) that plans 14 days of shifts, trading wages against guest wait time. Forecast errors run 12 to 19 points against 17 to 22 for the best simple baseline, and a challenger replaces the champion only if a bootstrap test says it's better. A synthetic-control study suggests Epic Universe cut Universal Studios' crowds by 20% to 30%, and an LLM agent answers questions from the forecast and optimizer, with every number checked against tool output.

cmapss-predictive-maintenance.title: Predictive Maintenance on a Governed Semantic Layer
cmapss-predictive-maintenance.result: Tandem XGBoost models flag turbofan engines 50 and 15 cycles before failure, catching about 91% of failures on held-out NASA C-MAPSS engines. One Snowflake semantic view feeds a report, Cortex Analyst and an MCP server under a read-only role, with all 80 metrics reconciled against hand-written SQL. Ported to Databricks as a Unity Catalog feature table, MLflow champion models, a Kedro pipeline registered as one model, and the metric views behind the live Genie app.

michelin-rag.title: Tire Industry Report Analyst
michelin-rag.result: A LangGraph agent that answers questions over 1,250 pages of tire-industry annual reports with page citations. It got 40 of 41 hand-checked questions right, then 82% of the 300 held-out questions in a harder 400-question test, which showed where it's weakest: comparisons (42%) and false premises (67%). It handled every off-topic and prompt-injection attempt in both tests.

snowpark-customer-segmentation.title: Customer Segmentation
snowpark-customer-segmentation.result: Segments 4,261 customers by predicted next-quarter value and buying style. The top 20% capture 71% of next-quarter revenue, against 56% for standard RFM. Includes Segment Assistant, an LLM chat app for exploring the segments.

semantic-rca.title: Automated Root Cause Analysis
semantic-rca.result: When a KPI drops, it works out why by crawling the dbt Semantic Layer in 8 to 11 warehouse statements, then splits the change across causes with Owen values and bootstrap intervals. On its showcase dataset it finds all four planted incidents with the right mechanism and sign. A benchmark over randomly planted incidents now scores recall and precision across many datasets, and is guiding the next round of improvements.

loan-default-prediction.title: Loan Default Prediction
loan-default-prediction.result: An ECOA-compliant model with an F2-tuned threshold that catches about 75% of defaults on a true holdout (AUC 0.76). Along the way it caught training-data leakage that had inflated the first estimate. It was rebuilt on Databricks, where one Optuna-tuned LightGBM matches the three-model ensemble (AUC 0.771 vs 0.762).

grid-stress-simulator.title: Grid Stress Simulator
grid-stress-simulator.result: Models how heat pump and EV adoption shift winter peak load across South Carolina counties. An 11 PM EV charging timer would create a new midnight peak above today's morning peak.

theme-park-event-extraction.title: Theme Park Event Extraction
theme-park-event-extraction.result: Finds parks, attractions, events and dates in text and turns them into proposed rows for a park events calendar, keeping the sentence as evidence. On 150 hand-labeled Wikipedia sentences, list-based rules score F1 0.76. DistilBERT fine-tuned on the rules' labels ties them (0.76 over three seeds) because it learns to copy them, and zero-shot GLiNER finds the most names missing from the rules' lists (40%), at about half their precision.
